Internals of arming, disarming, validation, lookup, optimization, trampoline handling and architecture helpers.
Module lifecycle, notifier registration, fault notification, sysctl exposure and credential visibility rules beyond what is shown.
Sequence, debugfs and file operation contracts beyond the wiring shown here.

findings.text: The lane exposes two operations to toggle an individual probe. Disabling reports success or a negative error. Enabling first validates the handle, rejects handles already marked gone, clears the disabled mark on an alias wrapper, and when the global switch is armed attempts to arm the underlying probe, restoring the disabled marks if arming fails.
A diagnostic operation reports a probe identity comprising its symbol name, numeric offset and resolved address through the kernel error log.

Two operations extend the probe blacklist. One registers a single kernel text address after resolving its containing symbol extent and returns that extent size or a negative error. The other walks an address interval symbol by symbol, advancing by each registration result.
A weak early initialization hook allows architecture code to contribute additional blacklist entries. The default implementation performs no work and reports success.
An operation scans the whole probe hash and retires every probe whose address lies inside the kernel init memory range which is being released.
A module load hook iterates the module memory classification and marks selected regions as excluded from leak scanning based on their type and protection attribute.
Once a probe is marked gone it stays gone. Enabling such a probe is rejected, and listing distinguishes gone from merely disabled.

A global boolean records whether all probes are disarmed. When set, individual enable requests only clear the alias mark and do not arm, while global arm clears the flag before attempting per probe arming.

Each blacklist entry covers a half open interval from a symbol start address up to start plus the symbol size discovered at insertion time. Removal deletes entries whose start lies inside a given range, including single address removal.
Area registration guarantees forward progress by advancing at least one address unit when a symbol lookup yields zero length, which handles aliased symbols.

Early blacklist population skips addresses that fail validation, aborts on other negative errors, always covers the dedicated probe and non instrumentable text ranges, and finally invokes the architecture hook, propagating its result.
Module attach and detach maintain the blacklist symmetrically. Explicit per module entries plus the module probe text and non instrumentable ranges are added on arrival and removed on departure.
Each supported module compression format validates a leading magic sequence before allocating decoder state. Mismatched input is rejected without producing output pages.

Decompressed output is collected as a growable array of page pointers with separate capacity and usage counts. Capacity is enlarged by the current usage amount when full, and total output length accumulates per page fill.
Retiring a probe requires the central probe mutex to be already held by the caller.

Single probe disable and enable, module notification handling, init memory reclamation, and global arm and disarm each hold the central probe mutex for their entire critical section via scoped acquisition.

Blacklist listing acquires the central mutex at sequence start and releases it at sequence stop, while live probe listing instead traverses the hash under read side protection with preemption disabled and without taking the mutex.

Observed probe state includes flag bits for gone, disabled, aggregated, optimized and tracing modes, a chaining list for aggregates, optional post handling, an address plus symbolic name and offset, and hash linkage. Aggregate probes head a list of chained probes.
Observed blacklist entries carry a start address, an end address, list linkage for ordered traversal, and deferred reclamation state allowing removal without blocking readers.
Observed module state relevant here includes an optional array of blacklist addresses with a count, plus optional base pointers and sizes for probe text and non instrumentable text regions.
Observed loader state for decompression includes a pointer array for output pages together with capacity and usage counts that the paging helpers maintain.

Probe listing is presented as a sequence over hash bucket indices with trivial stop, blacklist listing as a sequence over the blacklist with mutex protection, and the global switch as a file with read, write and seek handlers.

A probe moves among armed, disabled and gone. Single probe disable delegates to the internal disable path, enable clears the disabled indication and arms when globally armed, retiring marks gone and for aggregates also marks members gone, clears post handling and releases architecture state. Gone is terminal.

Module notification handling distinguishes three phases. Arrival adds blacklist coverage, live reclamation retires probes in the module init area, and departure retires probes in both init and core areas then drops module blacklist coverage. Other phases do nothing.

Global control is idempotent. Requesting the current state returns immediately, otherwise the global flag is flipped first and then every eligible probe is processed on a best effort basis with error and total tallies.

Decompression proceeds as acquire a page, decode into it, then account bytes, repeating until the decoder reports completion or failure. Success requires an explicit stream completion indication, and resources are released on all paths.

Early initialization sets up hash buckets, populates the blacklist with a warning on failure, resolves named return probe blacklist addresses with per name warnings, defaults the global switch to armed, initializes optimization and architecture support, subscribes to fault and module notifications, records overall success, and initializes sysctl exposure. A separate late hook triggers global optimization.
Debug interface creation establishes a directory for probes with three files: a read only live list, a read write global switch, and a read only blacklist view.

Probes anchored in memory that is about to be freed are retired without attempting to restore the original instruction, and optimized probes pending removal are diverted away from the optimizer path. Removed blacklist entries are reclaimed after a grace period.
Global arm and disarm may partially fail and leave a mixture of states while still reporting counts. Listings hide numeric addresses when the caller lacks permission to see them.

Decompression hazards include undersized or corrupt headers, decoder initialization failure, per page allocation failure, mid stream decode errors and oversized decompression windows. Each aborts with a negative error and releases decoder resources.

Gzip compressed modules are identified by a three byte prefix with hexadecimal values 1F, 8B and 08, followed by a flags byte whose file name bit selects an additional zero terminated name field that extends the header length beyond ten bytes.
Xz compressed modules are identified by a six byte prefix with hexadecimal values FD, 37, 7A, 58, 5A and 00.
Zstd compressed modules are identified by a four byte prefix with hexadecimal values 28, B5, 2F and FD, and the decoder rejects frames whose window exceeds the configured maximum.

The probe list and blacklist files use read only mode 0400, the enabled file uses owner read write mode 0600, and the enabled content is two byte text holding one plus newline when armed and zero plus newline when disarmed.
Live listing marks return probes with letter r and others with letter k, and appends bracketed tags for gone, disabled, optimized and tracing states.
Three build variants each pair a compression identity with its corresponding decompression routine, covering gzip, xz and zstd.

Module notification subscription has two build variants. One registers the probe notifier block and propagates its result, the other performs no work and reports success. The notifier block wires the module callback with priority zero.
